messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GeoDNS error rate exceeded threshold for api.redwood.com in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Symptoms: DNS timeouts and SERVFAIL observed from multiple public resolvers. Triggered at 2026-03-15T16:09:27Z. Severity: P1.

jane_oncall: Acked. I'm on it — grabbing context and runbook. Who's seeing metrics? :eyes:

sanjay_netops: I'm seeing spikes of SERVFAIL from Cloudflare resolvers in eu-west on our synthetic checks. Cloudflare Status page shows partial edge degradation around the same window (https://status.cloudflare.com).

maria_sre: Route53 health checks look fine for origins, but our GeoDNS control plane reports high latency when pushing zone updates to Route53 in us-east. TTLs still 300s for the zone - can't rely on fast re-propagation.

alex_platform: Customer-facing errors: increased 5xx on /v1/generate in eu-west and us-east due to DNS lookup failures to api.redwood.com. Spike started ~16:07Z, aligned with the pager.

jane_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) trigger GeoDNS failover to backup pool (ns-alt + different provider) 2) temporarily route affected regions to Dedicated endpoints with hardcoded IPs in our edge layer 3) contact Cloudflare support for edge resolver issue. Thoughts?

sanjay_netops: I can push failover on GeoDNS. Quick command (doing this in the thread for audit):
```
geodnsctl set-pool api.redwood.com --active-pool primary --fallback backup-pool --force-switch --reason "Edge resolver failures - immediate mitigation"
```
I'll run now if we agree.

maria_sre: +1 to failover. Also I'll prepare a resolver-harden step: spin up two regional resolvers and add them to our egress policy so services use them instead of public resolvers. That buys us time while CF investigates.

product_ops: Drafting status page blurb now. Will include affected regions + mitigation steps. TAG: customer-impact: some API requests may have returned DNS errors between 16:07-16:20Z.

support-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-332 created and linked to this thread. Notifying enterprise customers on the outage list now.

sanjay_netops: Executing failover command 16:12Z...

sanjay_netops: Done. GeoDNS control plane reports pool switch accepted. Propagation note: with Route53/Cloudflare there can still be resolver-level caching; full convergence expected within ~5-10m for most resolvers.

alex_platform: Observability: traffic shift seen to backup pool ~16:13Z. Errors down ~65% in eu-west, ~70% in us-east on 1min granularity. Showing dig checks:
```
; before
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com
; -> (timeout)
; after
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com
; -> 34.210.12.45
```
We're getting resolvable IPs again from public resolvers that hit the backup pool.

jane_oncall: Nice. Maria, can you confirm services are using our regional resolvers and not hitting the problematic edge resolvers?

maria_sre: Confirmed. Updated /etc/resolv.conf via chef for edge fleets in eu-west/us-east to point at our resolver pair. Sample check:
```
$ nslookup api.redwood.com 10.10.2.5
Server: 10.10.2.5
Address: 10.10.2.5#53
Name: api.redwood.com
Address: 34.210.12.45
```
All good.

product_ops: Status page draft: "We've detected DNS resolution issues affecting api.redwood.com in certain regions. We've failed over GeoDNS to a backup pool and resolution is returning to normal for most users. We're continuing to monitor and will provide updates." Shall I post?

jane_oncall: Post it. Add ETA for next update in 30m. Also set on-call handoff note: I'll be primary oncall for the next 45m then hand off to pager rotation (Sanjay).

support-bot: Customer notifications sent to enterprise list at 16:16Z.

sanjay_netops: Reached out to Cloudflare support (ticket CF-20260315-998). They replied acknowledging edge resolver queuing, investigating routing within their network. We should still treat as ongoing until they confirm root cause.

alex_platform: Monitoring: error rates now near baseline but a small tail remains for certain geographic resolvers (mobile carriers). We may want to keep backup pool for 1-2 hours before returning to primary to avoid flip-flop.

maria_sre: Agreed. Also capturing dig traces for postmortem: `dig +trace api.redwood.com` showed divergent answers from some ISP resolvers. Saving logs to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1861234567/dig-traces.txt

jane_oncall: Next steps summary: 1) Keep GeoDNS on backup pool for 60m 2) Maintain regional resolvers 3) Continue to press CF for RCA 4) Post-incident: evaluate TTLs, add more health-checks across public resolvers, and update runbook.

product_ops: Posted status page update and linked incident ticket.

support-bot: Noted. Slack notification sent to #customers-ops.

jane_oncall: Handing off monitoring to @sanjay_netops in 30m. If error rates climb >10% again, escalate to SEV2 and we re-open mitigation options.

sanjay_netops: Got it. I'll watch the tail and keep CF ticket active. If we need to, we can route via dedicated IPs at the edge layer as a hotfix.

maria_sre: I'll draft postmortem checklist and assign action items (TTL change plan, better public-resolver coverage tests).

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity set to P1 -> mitigated. Notes: GeoDNS failover executed; partial customer impact; follow-ups assigned.

jane_oncall: Wrapping up on my side. Thanks team. We'll compile timeline and RCA once CF confirms their side. :white_check_mark:
